messages.body_plain:
I would start with the documentation on connecting to a local database <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html#accessing-your-local-databases-from-shinyapps.io>.

Things to keep in mind are that you need to use a publicly accessible server name or IP address, that your database must accept connections from the IP addresses in the documentation, and that the FreeTDS version should be 7.2.

If you are still having problems, please share your connect command, with secrets replaced with "xxxx" or similar.

messages.subject_clean: Error: Repository must be specified for Bioconductor package source
messages.body_plain:
The manifest in the bundle that is uploaded is missing the repository information for the cellrangerRkit package.

Searching for that package, it appears to be nominally available only as a download <https://support.10xgenomics.com/single-cell/software/pipelines/latest/rkit>. We currently support installing packages <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/getting-started.html#using-your-r-packages-in-the-cloud> from CRAN, Bioconductor, and GitHub. It appears some folks have created their own GitHub <https://github.com/buenrostrolab/cellrangerRkit> repositories <https://github.com/hb-gitified/cellrangerRkit> with the package contents, but I could not comment about whether that is acceptable use.

messages.subject: Re: maximum size of the database
messages.subject_clean: maximum size of the database
messages.body_plain:
I presume you are asking about loading the data from these databases that you are hosting, as shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> doesn't provide a database itself. Alternatively, you might mean to store them as files that are uploaded with your application to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, in which case there is a limit <http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/applications.html> of 1 GB for free and starter plans, and up to 5 GB for the higher tiers.

With respect to capacity, the answer depends completely upon how much of the data you are loading into memory at any given time, and how efficiently it is being stored in memory. Basic plans and higher have access to instance types that provide up to 8GB of memory.

With respect to delays, there are latency and throughput "costs" to transferring data across the Internet that would contribute to a delay.

Hope that helps.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

My app works fine locally but not when deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>

This is the key code. It was written a couple of years ago but. as mentione, performs fine locally

The input data is from a reactive

output$wikiCard <- renderUI({
  req(data)

  theName <- str_replace_all(data()$vals[1]," ","_")
  url <- paste0("http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/",theName)
  test <- http_status(GET(url))

  if (test$category == "client error")
    return()

  vcard <- read_html(url) %>%
    html_nodes(".vcard")

  if (length(vcard) == 0)
    return()

  vcardInfo <- vcard[[1]]

  HTML(as(vcardInfo,"character"))
})

 uiOutput("wikiCard")

I raised this as a flexboard issue on github <https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/issues/107> but the suggestion of adding library(selectr) did not help

JJ states that this is a shinyapps issue

TIA

messages.body_plain:
Joshua,

In working with the Stan developers, they made changes to my project (so as to conform it to the way they do things). Furthermore, they recommended I install the package [on the shinyapps server] using the `args = --preclean` flag as is done in rstanarm <https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm>. The results are as follows:

With both `src/RescueTimeEstimator.so` and `src/Modules.o` omitted from the project, I am able to successfully install and run the package on a fresh Docker container running Ubuntu 14.04 (dmccloskey/r-base <https://hub.docker.com/r/dmccloskey/r-base/> image).

Additionally, this works for both:
`install_github("cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator", args = "--preclean", build_vignettes = FALSE)`
`install_github("cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator")`
Unfortunately, when I deploy to shinyapps, I get the same errors as before.
With the cache off, I get a message saying `Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 340213605 failed: Error building image: Error building RescueTimeEstimator (1.0)`, and nothing more.
Subsequently, with the cache then turned on, I get the same ELF header error as before.
I've attached both logs.

Crucially, with both `src/RescueTimeEstimator.so` and `src/Modules.o` now omitted from the project, the shinyapps server is tasked with two things:
Compiling the RStan code
Building the package
In my initial attempt a week ago - where I simply included the RStan code in my application project, and didn't build a separate R package as I'm doing now - the server was tasked with #1 just the same, and failed (presumably) because of a simple memory error. In fact, this is probably the simple reason the GitHub install is failing as well.

In all, I see 3 possible routes to get this thing to work:
Leave the Stan code in the application repository. This implies:
I would not make a separate R package to contain this Stan code, as I'm doing now (`cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator`).
When the Stan model is first run on the shinyapps server, it must be compiled by g++. This is what I tried in my initial attempt, and it failed for (presumably) a simple memory error.
Compile the Stan code in a Docker container running Ubuntu 14.04, then include the resulting `src/RescueTimeEstimator.so` and `src/Modules.o` in the GitHub repository. Results:
This resulted in "ELF header" errors on the shinyapps server, including after using the `elfedit` tool you recommended above.
On a fresh Docker container running Ubuntu 14.04, I can successfully install from GitHub using both:
`install_github("cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator", args = "--preclean", build_vignettes = FALSE)`
`install_github("cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator")`
Create an R package containing the Stan model, which is tasked at deploy with both compiling the Stan model in g++ then building the R package. Results:
As shown above. Solution: more memory.
In the first and third cases, the solution seems to simply be to acquire more memory. This said, I'd only need this memory for the 3 minutes it takes the model code to initial compile. Thereafter, the 1GB free-tier is more than sufficient. Of course, I could upgrade to a paid plan, but $40/month for a 3-minute use-case is out of my budget. :/

How do you recommend I proceed?

Continued thanks.

P.S. For reference, the related thread on the Stan forums can be found here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!category-topic/stan-users/general/HYs-dCCa2h0>.

messages.body_plain:
Per my earlier comment about not being packrat expert, you still have a bundle in the packrat subdirectory that contains the .so file built on the Mac.

The full logs for building RescueTimeEstimator are:

[2017-02-09T09:56:51.374894057+0000] Building R package: RescueTimeEstimator (1.0)

/mnt/packages/build /mnt
Warning in untar2(tarfile, files, list, exdir, restore_times) :

`all'.

installing to /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RescueTimeEstimator/libs
** R

Warning: /tmp/Rtmp78PKyP/R.INSTALLa32e3a6d6/cavaunpeu-RescueTimeEstimator-aa89703/man/RescueTimeEstimator-package.Rd:26: All text must be in a section
Warning: /tmp/Rtmp78PKyP/R.INSTALLa32e3a6d6/cavaunpeu-RescueTimeEstimator-aa89703/man/RescueTimeEstimator-package.Rd:27: All text must be in a section

*** installing help indices

Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
  unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RescueTimeEstimator/libs/RescueTimeEstimator.so':
  /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RescueTimeEstimator/libs/RescueTimeEstimator.so: invalid ELF header

Error: loading failed
Execution halted
ERROR: loading failed
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RescueTimeEstimator’

Given that it found nothing to do, I looked at what was actually downloaded from GitHub to build (for the task you mentioned, 340213605):

Downloading package from: https://codeload.github.com/cavaunpeu/RescueTimeEstimator/legacy.tar.gz/aa89703822250864c9da3240af44f9aa96428e8b

That would appear to have the RescueTimeEstimator.so and Modules.o files.

The giveaway here is the last part of the path, which is the Git sha indicating the commit, which is your initial commit.

While you do not need to bump the version every time, the particular commit installed locally is used when uploading your application to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> to make sure we are using the same version as what you have locally. If you change your package on GitHub, you need to install it locally before deploying the application.

On Thursday, February 9, 2017 at 7:17:53 AM UTC-5, William Wolf wrote:
> Joshua,
>
> In working with the Stan developers, they made changes to my project (so as to conform it to the way they do things). Furthermore, they recommended I install the package [on the shinyapps server] using the `args = --preclean` flag as is done in rstanarm <https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm>. The results are as follows:
>
> With both `src/RescueTimeEstimator.so` and `src/Modules.o` omitted from the project, I am able to successfully install and run the package on a fresh Docker container running Ubuntu 14.04 (dmccloskey/r-base <https://hub.docker.com/r/dmccloskey/r-base/> image).
>

That did it! This was not obvious to me: I was diligently pushing all updates to GitHub/master, as I figured that's where devtools::install_github pulls from.

As a post-mortem, was there any way for me to have verified what commit was being used?
For others with a similar problem, the `RescueTimeEstimator.so` and `Modules.o` files should not be included on GitHub. (These are the files that are generated when the Stan code is compiled into C++ code, but before the encompassing R package itself is built).
Thanks so much for your help. Here's the app <https://willwolf.shinyapps.io/rescue-time-estimation/>! (I still need to make a few tweaks, so it might be down when you go to check, heh.)

devtools::install_github installs the package once, it doesn't automatically notice updates, and rsconnect always captures the version you have locally, and shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> will use that version.

devtools::session_info will display the SHA of what is currently installed.

messages.subject: set.seed generates different outputs
messages.subject_clean: set.seed generates different outputs
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Apologies if this has been covered elsewhere - I did search.

I have some code that generates clusters using a stochastic process. Thus, I use set.seed(10) to get a consistent output. This works fine on my own computer, and works fine on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> side. The issue is that the results are not consistent across the two. I get different results if I run the same code from both sources, even in the same browser window.

My understanding is that I should get the same output in both cases. Any insights into why this might be occurring? Or even better - how to fix it?

Thanks in advance,

Damien

messages.body_plain:
Update:  I can sometimes get the Excel file to load by saving a failed Excel file, either with a new name or not, either in a new directory or not.   A user told me she tried loading her file and it failed to load and then she tried it again (evidently without touching it) and the file loaded into the Shiny app.

The error appears on uploading the file.   I looked at the shiny::fileInput function (below) but can't see where the error message would be generated.   Clues or solutions welcome!
##shiny::fileinput()
function (inputId, label, multiple = FALSE, accept = NULL, width = NULL)
{
    restoredValue <- restoreInput(id = inputId, default = NULL)
    if (!is.null(restoredValue) && !is.data.frame(restoredValue)) {
        warning("Restored value for ", inputId, " has incorrect format.")
        restoredValue <- NULL
    }
    if (!is.null(restoredValue)) {
        restoredValue <- toJSON(restoredValue, strict_atomic = FALSE)
    }
    inputTag <- tags$input(id = inputId, name = inputId, type = "file",
        style = "display: none;", `data-restore` = restoredValue)
    if (multiple)
        inputTag$attribs$multiple <- "multiple"
    if (length(accept) > 0)
        inputTag$attribs$accept <- paste(accept, collapse = ",")
    div(class = "form-group shiny-input-container", style = if (!is.null(width))
        paste0("width: ", validateCssUnit(width), ";"), label %AND%
        tags$label(label), div(class = "input-group", tags$label(class = "input-group-btn",
        span(class = "btn btn-default btn-file", "Browse...",
            inputTag)), tags$input(type = "text", class = "form-control",
        placeholder = "No file selected", readonly = "readonly")),
        tags$div(id = paste(inputId, "_progress", sep = ""),
            class = "progress progress-striped active shiny-file-input-progress",
            tags$div(class = "progress-bar")))
}
################################################

Thank you for getting back to me. I failed when trying to make a minimal reproducible example. Not because I couldn't make one, but because I couldn't reproduce the behaviour using simple R functions.

So this led me to dig a bit deeper. The function I am having troubles with is Rtsne, which generates different outputs on my side and on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> side. The package relies on Rcpp. First thing I did was to update the Rcpp to the latest version - lo and behold this changed my output (given the same seed)! However, interestingly it didn't change the output on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> side. I checked and the R version, and Rtsne and Rcpp package versions, are the same on both sides (my computer and shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>).

My current thinking is that I'm running OSX here, and presumably the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> R session(s) are being run on a different OS. This makes me think that the differences could lie deeper in the C++ side of things?

Any further advice would be welcome.

Damien

On Tuesday, 14 February 2017 16:51:33 UTC+1, Winston Chang wrote:

> Could you supply a minimal reproducible example to help us diagnose the issue?
>
> -Winston

> On Tue, Feb 14, 2017 at 6:04 AM, Damien Farine <stu...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Dear all,
> >
> > Apologies if this has been covered elsewhere - I did search.
> >
> > I have some code that generates clusters using a stochastic process. Thus, I use set.seed(10) to get a consistent output. This works fine on my own computer, and works fine on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> side. The issue is that the results are not consistent across the two. I get different results if I run the same code from both sources, even in the same browser window.
> >
> > My understanding is that I should get the same output in both cases. Any insights into why this might be occurring? Or even better - how to fix it?
> >
> > Thanks in advance,
> >
> > Damien

messages.subject: Re: will search engines index my shiny app?
messages.subject_clean: will search engines index my shiny app?
messages.body_plain:
We serve a robots.txt to prevent crawlers from trying to index because we found that they would cause applications to start up, but they would not actually perform the subsequent Ajax requests that would render content worthy of them indexing.

We have captured a feature on our backlog to allow for the creation of static content for an application that would be served to crawlers, but this work is not scheduled at this time.

> Hello,
>

If they will, does anyone know of a command or function to include in my shiny code to keep them from doing this?
>
> Will

messages.subject: Re: inconsistent file upload of Excel files to shiny--works locally but inconsistent on shinyapps.io INTERIM FIX
messages.subject_clean: inconsistent file upload of Excel files to shiny--works locally but inconsistent on shinyapps.io INTERIM FIX
messages.body_plain:
We think the issue has to do with encoding.   When we force UTF-8 encoding rather than default Windows encoding (e.g. https://help.surveygizmo.com/help/encode-an-excel-file-to-utf-8-or-utf-16) and use Excel 2016 macro to create the files, they all load without the error.   We were previously using Excel 2010; when we forced UTF-8 encoding programmatically in VBA, we still had files fail to load.  However, opening and saving the files (no changes) seemed to resolve the error.

This is not a satisfactory solution as we can't explain why our fix worked.   Will post again if we understand more.

messages.body_plain:
The "warning" about failing to parse app.R is the problem. Because of that, the dependencies are not discovered, and your deployed app does not have ggplot2 available to it.
Could you please open an issue in the rsconnect GitHub repo <https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect> and include your latest app.R?
It's a wild guess, but perhaps the data$Año and output$año are the trigger for the parsing problem, try changing to data$ano and output$ano and see if that helps.

messages.body_plain:

messages.subject: Re: Locale error while deploying in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Locale error while deploying in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
After days of struggling with the same problem, I finally discovered a solution that works for me.

My system locale was set to South African English. I tried changing it to US English in R. R would register the change, but if I tried to publish my app, the change in locale would not register and I would still get the error. I then came to the conclusion, that this way of changing the locale did not register when publishing. I had to manually change my locale in my computer's settings for the change to become permanent. For some reason, I had to change the system locale, as well as the system format to US English, before R registered the change in system locale. it was only then that the warning/error message disappeared after publishing.

Just a side note, my app still gave an internal server error after the system locale was changed, but this was due to a different reason (one of my .rds files was larger than 100mb, which I only later realised was not allowed https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/217717347-How-do-I-load-data-for-my-apps-on-shinyapps-io- ).

I finally got my app to publish, so I hope this piece of information helps someone who is still struggling with this issue.

Johannes
